answer: Each agent earns a reputation token called a nectar, minted only after it completes a signed task that a quorum of neighboring agents validates through a logical prism of consensus. The tokens decay linearly when the agent is idle, so an identity that appears suddenly without a long‑standing knoll of attestations lacks sufficient nectar to influence decisions. An attacker must therefore create many long‑lived, continuously active fake agents, incurring proportional computational and staking costs that grow with the desired influence.
